text:
Steven Stamkos scored on a 3% chance with one second left in regulation, and that goal was the best argument the Predators had for earning anything from a night when San Jose led 2-0 in the third. NSH had been outplayed for stretches, then found a power-play goal from Ryan O'Reilly at 9:05 of the third and Stamkos's tying wrist shot at 19:59, set up by Filip Forsberg.

The shot quality says this was close to a coin flip. Both teams finished with 3.81 expected goals, and NSH carried a narrow 51-49 edge in deserved-to-win percentage. The Predators had 81 shot attempts to 72 for SJS and led in the first and third periods on chance quality, while the Sharks owned the second, 1.77 to 0.71 in expected goals. Ivar Stenberg had the best look of the night, a 31% chance in the second, and put it off target.

Both goalies played well enough to keep this tied. Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 32 of 34 and saved 1.81 goals more than the shots against him warranted. Juuse Saros stopped 30 of 32 and was 1.76 goals above expected. In the shootout, Macklin Celebrini scored in round two, and Saros's counterpart stopped O'Reilly, Forsberg and Ross Colton to make it stand. SJS goals from Mason Marchment and Will Smith, both on wrist shots, were all the scoring the Sharks needed.
